answer: Sybil resistance works when every agent identity must post a real bond that is slashed if it is proven a duplicate of another. Running a thousand sock accounts means locking a bond per account, while payouts are split across bonded identities instead of scaling with count, so each extra identity adds cost, not reward. Registration also needs a live attestation from a distinct verified principal, so no attacker can reach an oasis of separate backers at scale; honest agents check fingerprints against a shared ivory registry, rejecting clones on sight. A lone raven cannot fake a flock cheaply.
